messages:
Oncall Bot: INCIDENT detected: serving-pool-3 experiencing repeated container OOMs and CUDA context resets on node gpu-12. Autoscaler triggered but pods failing to come up. Alerts: high kv_cache pager fragmentation and slow resident growth.
Infra SRE: seeing repeated errors in kube logs: `E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda_driver.cc:704] driver shutting down` then container SIGKILL from OOM killer. stack: 
```
E CudaDriver: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION
E /srv/runtime/allocator: kv_paged_alloc failed: out of memory
Killed process 1823 (serve) total-vm: 486000kB
```
Alice: I'm taking the node out of rotation (kubectl cordon gpu-12) and will drain pods from that node to distribute load. starting drain now.
Ben: on it — re-routing traffic for heavy customers to fallback model group `redwood-small-quant` to reduce memory pressure. I pushed a temporary route rule.
Carmen: customer-facing ops: we've seen 5 distinct VIP customers with 500/503s in the last 12m, highest impact window ~6151239900-6151240100. Preparing status page blurb: "We are investigating intermittent 503s affecting model serving; mitigation in progress."
David: scale request to Dedicated pool queued (requested +2 gpus). Also bumping eviction aggressiveness on serving runtime: `--kv-evict-threshold=0.65` -> currently 0.8, lowering to 0.65 will evict earlier. Will monitor.
Eva: recommending a one-off compaction run on the largest kv-shards before we re-populate cache: `sudo /opt/redwood/bin/kv-compact --shard=17 --max-ttl=600` — compaction should reduce fragmentation. Scheduling now on a maintenance node.
Infra SRE: running quick check of fragmentation metrics: resident pages per shard trending: [shard17: 74% -> 88%], fragmentation ratio 0.62 -> 0.78 over 48h. This is slow creep pattern (paged allocator small-slab churn). Looks like small allocations not coalescing, KCACHE warm paths holding stale refs.
Alice: drain completed. restarted 3 pods with `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=30`. two pods restarted cleanly, one failed with the same CUDA context reset. collecting /var/log/serve/stdout for that pod.
Ben: fallback route is live for high-traffic customers, saw immediate drop in OOMs on other nodes. throughput slightly lower but more stable.
Oncall Bot: Severity escalated to SEV2 due to customer impact and multiple failing pods.
Carmen: status page updated and sent to comms — included ETA: investigating, mitigation rolling out. No ETA for full resolution.
David: while compaction runs, enabling KV conservative GC on the runtime (`--kv-conservative-gc=true`) to avoid aggressive per-request allocations. Also disabling long prefix caching for chat-heavy routes temporarily.
Eva: compaction finished for shard17, reclaimed ~4.6GB, fragmentation down to 0.58. Pushing compaction to next 3 largest shards sequentially (to avoid IO spike).
Infra SRE: after compaction and eviction threshold change, remaining nodes show reduced pressure. One noisy pod still logs `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT` right before OOM — might be a driver edge case. I'm rolling a driver update on a test node (nvidia-driver 535.86 -> 536.10) and will validate.
Deploy Bot: restarted container serve-8 on node gpu-14: SUCCESS (uptime 00:02:30). No OOM since restart.
Alice: temporary mitigation checklist: 1) cordon + drain gpu-12 (done) 2) route heavy customers to fallback (done) 3) run sequential compaction on top shards (in progress) 4) lower kv-evict threshold (done) 5) driver update test (in progress).
Ben: monitoring token-level cost and latency — fallback adds ~12% latency but keeps SLA. Metrics dashboard linked: https://console/redwood/metrics/incidents/6151239876
Carmen: comms sent to 7 affected customers with note about degraded availability and our mitigation steps; asked for impact reports. One customer replied: "We saw 15 failed calls over 20m but degraded to fallback worked, thanks."
David: request infra-sre to schedule controlled node driver rollout after confirmation on test node. If driver update doesn't help, we may need a runtime patch for the CUDA hijack during slab coalescing.
Infra SRE: test node with driver 536.10 passed a 6h soak with no context resets under load profile. Planning staged rollout to 4 nodes in the pool starting in 15m.
Eva: post-incident action item: add scheduled compaction to autoscale lifecycle when fragmentation > 0.6 and resident growth rate > 1%/h. Also add eviction tuning per model group.
Alice: if things remain stable for 30m we'll de-escalate. For now keeping SEV2 and tracking.
Oncall Bot: Incident refresh: mitigation effective, customer impact reduced. Next update planned in 20 minutes.
Deploy Bot: driver rollout to nodes [gpu-05,gpu-09,gpu-14,gpu-18] started.
Carmen: posting summary to incident channel and creating customer follow-up template for SRE + Sales.
Alice: closing note: root likely slow kv-paged fragmentation plus an unlucky driver interplay triggering context resets under OOM pressure. Actions assigned: driver rollout, scheduled compaction, conservative GC default, autoscale compaction trigger, and runtime patch investigation.
Oncall Bot: Incident closed to monitoring at 6151240450 — move to postmortem phase when logs and metrics are collected.
